question: What is the best way to start a sprint race to get maximum speed? 🏁
answer: Crouch start (getting low) 🏃
explanation: Awesome! A crouch start helps you push off the ground with more power and helps you reach top speed quickly! 🏃
hint: You need to be low to the ground to explode forward.

question: Which commands are used for a crouch start in a short sprint? 📢
answer: On your marks, Set, Go! 🔫
explanation: Great job! These three commands help athletes get into the perfect position before exploding off the starting line. 🔫
hint: Think about what the referee says before blowing the whistle.

question: How should your arms move when you are sprinting fast? 💪
options: Pumping forward and backward at a 90-degree angle 🏃
Held straight up in the air 🙋
answer: Pumping forward and backward at a 90-degree angle 🏃
explanation: Excellent! Pumping your arms forward and backward helps drive your legs faster and keeps your body balanced! 🏃
hint: Your arms should move like the wheels of a fast train.

question: In a running race, which direction do athletes always run around the track? 🏟️
answer: Anti-clockwise (counter-clockwise) 🔄
explanation: Brilliant! Standard track and field rules state that all running events happen in an anti-clockwise direction around the track. 🔄
hint: It is the opposite direction of how a clock's hands move.

question: Why is it important to stay in your own lane during a 100-meter sprint? 🛣️
options: To avoid bumping into other runners 🏃‍♂️
answer: To avoid bumping into other runners 🏃‍♂️
explanation: Fantastic! Staying in your lane keeps the race safe and fair for everyone, preventing any accidental collisions! 🏃‍♂️
hint: Think about driving a car safely on a highway.

question: What is the very first phase of the Long Jump event? 🦘
answer: Approach Run 🏃
explanation: Super! The approach run is the first step, where you build up the speed needed to jump really far! 🏃
hint: You have to run fast before you can jump.

question: In the Long Jump, what happens if your foot crosses the take-off line before you jump? ❌
options: It is called a foul jump 🚫
answer: It is called a foul jump 🚫
explanation: Spot on! Your foot must stay behind the take-off line to make the jump fair and legal. It's a great rule to practice! 🚫
hint: It is like stepping out of bounds in a game.

question: What is the safest way to land in a Long Jump pit? 🏖️
answer: On both feet, falling forward 🤸
explanation: Wonderful! Landing on both feet and falling forward keeps you safe and ensures you get the best possible measurement! 🤸
hint: You want your momentum to carry you to the front, not the back.

question: What is the heavy metal ball used in throwing events called? 🥎
answer: Shot put 🥎
explanation: Great! The shot put is a heavy metal ball that athletes push as far as they can using strength and technique. 🥎
hint: It sounds like you are 'putting' a 'shot'.

question: How should you correctly hold the shot put before throwing it? ✋
options: In the palm of your hand 🖐️
With two hands like a basketball 🏀
At the base of your fingers 🤌
Squeezing it with your thumb only 👍
answer: At the base of your fingers 🤌
explanation: Excellent! Holding the shot put at the base of your fingers gives you the best flick and pushing power when you release it! 🤌
hint: Keep it off the palm to give it a strong push.

question: Where do you rest the shot put right before you make your throw? 👤
options: Against your neck, close to your jaw/chin 🗣️
answer: Against your neck, close to your jaw/chin 🗣️
explanation: Awesome! Resting it snugly against your neck and jaw helps transfer all your body's power directly into the throw! 🗣️
hint: Tuck it safely under your chin.

question: What is the golden rule of releasing the shot put? 🥇
options: Push it away from your neck 🚀
answer: Push it away from your neck 🚀
explanation: Fantastic! The shot put is an exploding 'push' rather than a normal throw, which protects your arm and gives maximum distance! 🚀
hint: Imagine pushing a heavy door open quickly.

question: What is the correct way to exit the throwing circle after a shot put throw? 🚶
options: Walk out from the back half of the circle 🔙
Do a cartwheel out the side 🤸
answer: Walk out from the back half of the circle 🔙
explanation: Brilliant! Walking out from the back of the circle shows the referee that you are finished and keeps your throw valid! 🔙
hint: Always retreat the way you came in.

question: What is the most important safety rule during any throwing event? 🛡️
options: Make sure nobody is standing in the landing sector 🚷
Throw as fast as you can without looking 👀
answer: Make sure nobody is standing in the landing sector 🚷
explanation: Excellent! Safety first! Always check that the field is completely clear before you make your mighty throw. 🚷
hint: You need an empty space for the object to land safely.

question: What object do athletes pass to each other during a Relay Race? 🔀
answer: A baton 🪄
explanation: Super! A baton is a smooth, hollow tube that runners carefully hand off to their teammates in a relay race. 🪄
hint: It looks like a short, colorful stick.

question: How many athletes make up a standard relay team on the track? 🏃‍♂️🏃‍♀️
answer: Four 🖖
explanation: Awesome! A standard relay team consists of four fast runners working perfectly together to complete the race! 🖖
hint: Think of a 4x100 meter race.

question: Where must the baton be passed between runners in a relay race? 🔲
answer: Inside the exchange zone 🔲
explanation: Great job! The exchange zone is a marked area of 20 meters where the baton must be passed safely to the next runner. 🔲
hint: It is a specific 'box' marked by lines on the track.

question: What should you do if you accidentally drop the baton during a relay race? 😲
options: The athlete who dropped it must safely pick it up 🪄
answer: The athlete who dropped it must safely pick it up 🪄
explanation: Fantastic! Mistakes happen! You just safely pick it up and keep running your hardest for your team! 🪄
hint: You can't finish the race without it, so you must get it back safely.

question: What is the 'flight' phase in jumping events? ✈️
options: The time your body is traveling through the air 🦅
answer: The time your body is traveling through the air 🦅
explanation: Brilliant! The flight phase is that awesome moment when you are soaring through the air like a bird! 🦅
hint: Think about what airplanes do.

question: Which body part must cross the finish line first to win a running race? 🎽
answer: The torso (chest) 🎽
explanation: Excellent! The race is officially finished when your torso (your chest area) crosses the finish line. Keep pushing through! 🎽
hint: It is the main middle part of your body where your heart is.

question: What is 'pacing' in middle and long-distance running? ⏱️
options: Sprinting as fast as you can immediately 🚀
Distributing your energy evenly over the whole race 🔋
answer: Distributing your energy evenly over the whole race 🔋
explanation: Super! Good pacing means saving enough energy so you can run strongly from the starting line all the way to the finish! 🔋
hint: It is like making sure your phone battery lasts the whole day.

question: Which of these is the best way to warm up before participating in Athletics? 🤸
answer: Light jogging and stretching 🏃‍♂️
explanation: Awesome! A great warm-up gets your blood flowing, prepares your muscles, and prevents injuries so you can do your best! 🏃‍♂️
hint: You need to get your body moving gently first.

question: What is the goal of the High Jump event? ⬆️
options: To jump as far forward as possible 🦘
To jump over a horizontal bar without knocking it down 📏
To jump over a puddle of water 💧
answer: To jump over a horizontal bar without knocking it down 📏
explanation: Great job! The high jump is all about leaping gracefully over a high bar and landing safely on the mat! 📏
hint: You want to go UP, not just FORWARD.

question: How many attempts does an athlete usually get to clear a specific height in the High Jump? 🔢
answer: Three 🤟
explanation: Fantastic! Athletes get three chances to clear the bar at each height, giving them a great opportunity to succeed! 🤟
hint: It is one more than two.

question: Why do athletes wear special shoes called 'spikes' for running on a track? 👟
options: To grip the track and prevent slipping 🛤️
answer: To grip the track and prevent slipping 🛤️
explanation: Excellent! The small metal pins on the bottom of the shoes grip the track, giving runners amazing traction and speed! 🛤️
hint: Think of how tires on a car grip the road.

question: What is a 'false start' in a sprint race? 🚫
options: Starting after the gun goes off 🔫
Moving or running before the starter's signal 🏃‍♂️
answer: Moving or running before the starter's signal 🏃‍♂️
explanation: Super! You must wait patiently for the 'Go!' signal. Moving too early is a false start, and waiting shows great discipline! 🏃‍♂️
hint: It means starting the race too early.

question: In the Long Jump, where is the measurement taken from? 📏
options: From where the athlete started running 🏃
From the take-off board to the closest mark made in the sand 🏖️
From the take-off board to the furthest handprint ✋
From the middle of the pit 🕳️
answer: From the take-off board to the closest mark made in the sand 🏖️
explanation: Brilliant! The jump is measured from the board to the mark in the sand closest to it. That's why falling forward is a great technique! 🏖️
hint: The officials look for the mark closest to the take-off line.

question: What should an athlete do immediately after completing a hard race to recover? 🚶
options: Do a cool-down jog and stretch gently 🧘
answer: Do a cool-down jog and stretch gently 🧘
explanation: Awesome! Cooling down gradually helps your heart rate return to normal and prevents your muscles from getting sore! 🧘
hint: You need to slow down your body step by step.

question: What is the best angle to release a throwing object for maximum distance? 📐
answer: Around 45 degrees ↗️
explanation: Great job! A 45-degree angle perfectly balances height and forward speed, making your throw go incredibly far! ↗️
hint: It is exactly halfway between straight out and straight up.

question: During a relay race, what is the best way to receive the baton from your teammate? 🫴
options: Running with your hand stretched back, trusting your teammate to place it in your hand 🏃‍♂️
answer: Running with your hand stretched back, trusting your teammate to place it in your hand 🏃‍♂️
explanation: Fantastic! A 'blind' exchange where you look forward and run fast while reaching back makes the team super fast! 🏃‍♂️
hint: You shouldn't slow down to take the stick.

question: Which of these is considered a 'Track' event in Athletics? 🏃‍♀️
answer: 100-meter sprint 🏁
explanation: Excellent! 'Track' events are the running races that happen on the oval running track! 🏁
hint: Track events involve running.

question: Which of these is considered a 'Field' event in Athletics? 🏟️
answer: Long Jump 🦘
explanation: Super! 'Field' events involve jumping and throwing, and they take place on the grassy field inside the track! 🦘
hint: This event involves a sand pit.

question: What is the proper breathing technique while running a long distance? 🫁
options: Breathe rhythmically using both nose and mouth 😮‍💨
answer: Breathe rhythmically using both nose and mouth 😮‍💨
explanation: Brilliant! Rhythmic breathing helps get plenty of oxygen to your muscles so you can keep running strong! 😮‍💨
hint: You need to take steady, deep breaths.

question: Why do high jumpers use a thick landing mat (crash mat)? 🛏️
options: To bounce back over the bar 🪀
For a safe and soft landing after a high jump 🛡️
To take a nap during the competition 😴
To make the jump look higher ⬆️
answer: For a safe and soft landing after a high jump 🛡️
explanation: Awesome! Safety is the top priority, and the thick mat protects jumpers from getting hurt when they land! 🛡️
hint: It provides a soft cushion for your back.

question: In athletics, what is the 'Take-off board' made of? 🪵
answer: Wood or synthetic material 🪵
explanation: Great job! The board is firm and flat, providing a solid surface for the athlete's foot to safely push off for a huge jump! 🪵
hint: It needs to be a hard, flat surface that isn't slippery.

question: What does a good 'stance' (body position) do for a thrower before they throw the shot put? 🧍‍♂️
options: It gives them perfect balance and prepares their muscles for power ⚖️
It helps them hide from the referee 🙈
answer: It gives them perfect balance and prepares their muscles for power ⚖️
explanation: Fantastic! A strong, balanced stance is the secret to generating massive power from your legs to your arms! ⚖️
hint: A strong building needs a strong foundation.

question: What happens if a runner crosses into another runner's lane and blocks them? 🚧
options: They can be disqualified for interfering 🚫
They get to run a shorter race 📏
answer: They can be disqualified for interfering 🚫
explanation: Excellent! Athletics is all about fairness. Blocking another runner is against the rules, so staying in your lane is best! 🚫
hint: Think about fairness in sports.

question: When running hurdles, what is the best technique to get over the barrier? 🚧
options: Jump high into the sky like a kangaroo 🦘
Step or glide over it quickly without losing running speed 🏃
answer: Step or glide over it quickly without losing running speed 🏃
explanation: Super! Hurdling is actually a 'sprint over an obstacle'. Gliding over keeps your forward momentum going fast! 🏃
hint: You want to clear it quickly and keep your speed.

question: What is the final part of a race called when you run your absolute hardest to the end? 🏁
answer: The finishing kick or sprint 🏃‍♂️💨
explanation: Brilliant! The 'finishing kick' is when you use all your remaining energy to power through the finish line like a champion! 🏃‍♂️💨
hint: It involves speeding up right at the very end.

question: Which foot should you use to jump off the board in the Long Jump? 🦶
options: Both feet at the same time 👣
answer: Your strongest foot (take-off foot) 🚀
explanation: Awesome! Using your strongest leg gives you the most powerful push into the air for a super long jump! 🚀
hint: Use the leg that gives you the most power.

question: During a sprint, where should your eyes be focused? 👀
options: Straight ahead on your lane and the finish line 🏁
answer: Straight ahead on your lane and the finish line 🏁
explanation: Great job! Looking straight ahead keeps your body perfectly aligned and focused on your goal! 🏁
hint: Keep your head up and look where you want to go.

question: What should you do if you feel very thirsty during a long sports practice? 💧
options: Take small sips of water to stay hydrated 🚰
Drink a large sports drink in one gulp 🥤
answer: Take small sips of water to stay hydrated 🚰
explanation: Fantastic! Hydration is key! Small sips of water keep your body working smoothly without making your stomach feel heavy. 🚰
hint: Your body needs fluids, but not too much all at once.

question: What is the best way to show good sportsmanship after an Athletics race? 🤝
options: Shake hands and say 'good race' to your competitors 🤝
answer: Shake hands and say 'good race' to your competitors 🤝
explanation: Excellent! A true champion always respects their competitors. Good sportsmanship is the best part of any sport! 🤝
hint: Treat others how you would want to be treated.

question: What shape does the run-up for the High Jump look like? 🔄
answer: A 'J' curve (straight then curved) ⤴️
explanation: Super! Running in a 'J' curve helps the athlete lean away from the bar and flip their hips gracefully over it! ⤴️
hint: It looks like a hook or the letter J.

question: Why do sprinters run on the balls of their feet (front part)? 🦶
options: It helps them bounce forward faster with less ground contact ⚡
Because their shoes are too big 👟
answer: It helps them bounce forward faster with less ground contact ⚡
explanation: Brilliant! Running on the balls of your feet acts like a spring, launching you forward incredibly fast! ⚡
hint: It minimizes the time your foot spends on the ground.

question: What does a 'Standing Broad Jump' test? 🦘
options: Your explosive leg power without a running start 🚀
How long you can stand on one leg 🦩
answer: Your explosive leg power without a running start 🚀
explanation: Awesome! This jump is a fantastic way to see how much powerful spring you have in your legs from a standstill! 🚀
hint: It tests how far you can jump from a stationary position.

question: In a relay race, the runner holding the baton is called the incoming runner. What is the one receiving it called? 🏃
answer: The outgoing runner 🏃‍♂️💨
explanation: Great job! The outgoing runner takes the baton and speeds off to continue the great work of the team! 🏃‍♂️💨
hint: They are going OUT onto the track.

question: What type of clothing is best suited for practicing Athletics? 🎽
options: Lightweight, breathable sports clothes and running shoes 🎽
answer: Lightweight, breathable sports clothes and running shoes 🎽
explanation: Fantastic! Comfortable sports clothes let your body move freely and keep you cool while you exercise! 🎽
hint: You need to be able to stretch and sweat comfortably.

question: When throwing a softball for distance, stepping forward with the opposite foot of your throwing arm does what? ⚾
options: Creates a powerful twist in your body to throw further 🌪️
answer: Creates a powerful twist in your body to throw further 🌪️
explanation: Excellent! Stepping with the opposite foot turns your hips and shoulders, adding massive twisting power to your throw! 🌪️
hint: It helps your body act like a coiled spring.

question: What is the ultimate goal of learning Fundamental Sports Skills in Class 6? 🌟
options: To build a healthy, active lifestyle and have fun 🏃‍♂️😊
answer: To build a healthy, active lifestyle and have fun 🏃‍♂️😊
explanation: Super! Learning these skills helps you stay fit, make friends, and enjoy the wonderful world of sports for your whole life! 🏃‍♂️😊
hint: Think about health and happiness.
